summary: Three medium findings: the instructed relocation of the normalization node leaves an inherited AG2.5-to-AG2.4 prerequisite against the stage order; the R14.6-to-R19.1 and IHG.4-to-AG2.4 ownership handoffs still lack routes in the accepted graph. The latter two are coordinated residuals of already confirmed area findings, not newly discovered mathematics. All sixteen layers and their substantive targets survive, all thirty proposal links are live, and the current assembled graph is acyclic. The proposed repairs are jointly acyclic. No return to the rejected linear-extension model is requested.
checked: At repository base 7882cb661ace64d038d4ed2ece955a438a088491, read the whole accepted RS-12.result.json, RS-12.md, RS-12~3 handoff and REV-RS-12~3 report, the ten family evidence rows, both member README files, all sixteen layer decisions, twenty owner records and thirty links.

Read all fifteen integrated decomposition nodes, twelve links, sixteen coverage entries and fifteen explicit gaps across the two members. Checked the normalization and geometric-congruence nodes and their prerequisites in the partial blueprint packets; inventoried the other packet nodes without treating unreviewed packets as accepted replacements.

Read the sixteen member entries in data/library-coverage.json and the AUDIT-31 accepted-review metadata. Read Representation, trivial, trivial_apply and the group-action elementary lemmas in Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Basic.lean at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. These have no continuity hypothesis. No new exhaustive library-absence claim is made; Tau Ceti remains pinned at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369.

Checked every external owner contract named by the proposal, including AF.4, R01.1/G7, IHG.1/3/4, R24.5:operations, R34.6 and IG.5; checked R14.3/R14.6 and ET.6 for the disputed boundaries. Read the contracts of all twenty-four distinct external consumers of the sixteen layers.

Fresh assemble(require_distances=False): 2907 stage/node records, 8322 distinct directed edges, acyclic. All thirty proposal links are present. Twenty-eight member-to-external export edges reach twenty-four consumers. All seventeen supplier-forwarding checks for narrowed stages pass even when the narrowed stage is removed from the tested path.

Checked the early raw-cohomology/local-correspondence frontier: no late AG2 stage reaches R19 and no R19 stage reaches AG2.0 or AG2.1a. Removing R16.6 -> R19.1 and R16.3 -> R16.6 still leaves AG2.1a -> ET.6 -> R17.2 -> R17.3 -> R19.2 and onward to R19.3-R19.6.

Projected the twelve inherited decomposition links onto their parent stages. The original placement is acyclic. Applying the required normalization relocation to AG2.5 introduces AG2.5 -> AG2.4 against AG2.4 -> AG2.5. Routing the construction's convention input through early AG2.0 and ET.6 removes that defect; adding both missing supplier routes simultaneously remains acyclic.

Public primary-source checks on 2026-10-01: HLTT author PDF, Theorem A and introduction pp. 1-3, section 6.1 pp. 194-197 (Lemma 6.2, Corollaries 6.3-6.4 and Proposition 6.5); Deligne Bourbaki 355, page images of Proposition 4.8 and Theorem 4.9, printed pp. 166-167; Varma arXiv:1411.2520, pp. 1-2. Source versions, hashes, scope and short quotations are in the report.

Compared the two residual ownership defects with confirmed RT-AREA-langlands-2/9 and RT-AREA-langlands-1/26 and their existing fixes reports. The partial R19 packet already names the R14.6 node, so the finding concerns the uncompleted stage/owner handoff, not a missing mathematical construction everywhere.

Preserved source scopes: weight one remains separate from regular-algebraic existence; higher-weight projectors use R14.3's carrier; full rank-two WD comparison is not replaced by nonselfdual monodromy bounds; coefficient-prime claims retain their branch hypotheses; raw cohomology does not import torsion concentration. The already recorded ordinary-elliptic-curve fibre correction and Steinberg/principal-series correction are not new findings. No Tau Ceti roadmap or link between Tau Ceti roadmaps changes.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-12.result.json layers[AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.0].reason; RS-12.md section 4a; inherited normalization-node -> HLTT-node link in data/decompositions/AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII.json
findings.claim: The required move of AG2.0/the-normalization-dictionary-fixed-by-the-sources to AG2.5 does not reconcile its outgoing prerequisite to AG2.4/hltt-construction-of-nonselfdual-systems. That edge also remains a literal prerequisite in the partial AG2.0 packet. If retained when the parent changes, it projects to AG2.5 -> AG2.4, while AG2.4 -> AG2.5 is already the construction-before-comparison order. The accepted stage graph is acyclic today; this is a defect in the instructed node migration, not a claim that its current stage graph has a cycle.
findings.evidence: RS-12's AG2.0 reason: 'The source-normalization comparison ... goes to AG2.5.' The inherited link's reviewer annotation says the node 'supplies no further mathematical input'. Its endpoints are AG2.0/the-normalization-dictionary-fixed-by-the-sources and AG2.4/hltt-construction-of-nonselfdual-systems. HLTT, https://www.kwlan.org/articles/rigcoh.pdf, Theorem A p. 1 (read 2026-10-01), states the construction at good primes with rec(pi_v |det|_v^((1-n)/2)); after the theorem: 'Here recEv denotes the local Langlands correspondence for Ev.' ET.6 already supplies that local correspondence before AG2.4. Fresh parent-projection test: inherited links plus stages are acyclic before relocation and cyclic after this relocation, with witness AG2.4 -> AG2.5 -> AG2.4.
findings.fix: Extend RS-12's placement instruction to cover the outgoing link and the partial packet's corresponding prerequisite. Split out the convention input: AG2.4 consumes AG2.0's rec-free Hecke/Frobenius dictionary together with ET.6's established local correspondence and its good-prime normalization. Keep the later comparison assertion under AG2.5 as an output after AG2.4, and remove the late comparison node as an input to HLTT. Preserve the source statement and its good-prime hypotheses. Check parent-projected node dependencies as well as the stage graph when applying all placement changes. Make the eventual plan repair in the owning blueprint, with reviewed promotion; do not patch the reviewed base decomposition by hand.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-12.result.json R19.1 keep reason/owners/links versus accepted RS-06 ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6 ownership
findings.claim: R19.1's retained geometric Eichler-Shimura construction is not explicitly narrowed to importing R14.6's already-owned special-fibre weight-two relation, and no R14.6 -> R19.1 path exists. The third review correctly supplied R14.3's universal-family carrier, but that is a different export from R14.6's relation. This is the still-uncompleted accepted-graph portion of confirmed RT-AREA-langlands-2/9. The partial R19 blueprint already names R14.6/special-fibre-eichler-shimura as a prerequisite; it has no R14.6 request and has not replaced the accepted graph.
findings.evidence: Accepted RS-06 R14.6 keeps 'the special-fibre Eichler-Shimura relation'; the current R14.6 document says 'Supply the special-fibre Eichler–Shimura relation'. RS-12 R19.1 retains the 'geometric Eichler-Shimura polynomial' while expressly naming only R14.3 for the modular-curve handoff. AUDIT-31's R19.1 duplicate record identifies R14.6 as this supplier. Deligne, https://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1968-1969__11__139_0.pdf, Proposition 4.8/Theorem 4.9, printed pp. 166-167 (images read 2026-10-01): 'T_p = F + I_p^* V', with FV = p^(k+1) on Sym^k cohomology. This separates the weight-two k=0 input from the higher-coefficient extension. Fresh graph: no R14.6 -> R19.1 path; adding it is acyclic. RT-AREA-langlands-2.review.json confirms /9; its fixes report already specifies this same remaining route.
findings.fix: Coordinate with RT-AREA-langlands-2/9 rather than commission another proof. Explicitly import R14.6's weight-two special-fibre relation in the RS-12 R19.1 ownership boundary and add the R14.6 -> R19.1 route. Complete the existing owning packet's R14.6 request and preserve its node prerequisite. R19.1 retains the eigenspace deduction, normalization and higher Sym^(weight-2)-coefficient congruence. Do not move the whole higher-weight realization into R14.6 or conflate R14.3's carrier with the relation. Apply through the owning blueprint/review workflow.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-12.result.json owner record for IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.4, AG2.4 keep reason and links
findings.claim: The proposal assigns generic finite-quotient interpolation to IHG.4 and explicitly lists AG2.4 as a former owner, but supplies its link only to R19.6. There is no direct or transitive IHG.4 -> AG2.4 route. Thus AG2.4's instruction to import the generic determinant API is not backed by the accepted prerequisite graph. This is the interpolation portion of already confirmed RT-AREA-langlands-1/26, still outstanding at this base; it does not request the downstream Scholze torsion construction.
findings.evidence: RS-12 owner target: 'Generic polynomial-law finite-quotient interpolation with continuity and integral congruence hypotheses', owner IHG.4, formerly including AG2.4. IHG.4's document begins 'Construct compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems'. HLTT, https://www.kwlan.org/articles/rigcoh.pdf, section 6.1, Lemma 6.2, Corollaries 6.3-6.4 and Proposition 6.5, pp. 195-197 (read 2026-10-01), passes from classical Hecke data to finite coefficient quotients and then the integral limit; p. 195 explicitly invokes 'the Cebotarev density theorem'. Its finite generated Hecke-stable modules, fixed ramification set and continuity are substantive inputs to match. Fresh graph: IHG.4 reaches R19.6 but not AG2.4. RT-AREA-langlands-1.review.json /26 confirms that AG2.4 should apply IHG.4 to its own congruence data; its fixes report already requests the missing edge.
findings.fix: Add IHG.4 -> AG2.4 to the proposal's handoff links and an explicit IHG.4 request/prerequisite in the owning AG2.4 blueprint. Keep the actual HLTT geometry, congruence estimates, finite-module/continuity checks, coefficient conventions and descent there; use IHG.4 for the generic interpolation and limit theorem. Check the trace-pseudorepresentation to determinant interface on the source's coefficient domain rather than infer integrality from density alone. Coordinate this with RT-AREA-langlands-1/26. Its separate factor-separation request still needs its own hypothesis matching; importing all of TC.3 or a torsion-concentration endpoint is not this repair.
